messages:
Morgan: did a quick kernel sweep + draft-pairing smoke across llama-3b, mistral-xl, mixtral-8x, qwen-7 this morning — summary below. noticed a perf regression when pairing llama drafts with mixtral-family decoders, and a weird acceptance drop tied to tokenizer alignment.
Priya: can you paste the numbers? p95 / p99 and acceptance rates pls
Morgan: quick table (representative):
```
model pairing         | kernel         | batch | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | accept_rate
llama3b->mixtral8     | flash_attn_v2  | 4     | 72      | 180     | 0.22
llama3b->mixtral8     | flash_attn_v1  | 4     | 88      | 220     | 0.23
mistral-xl native     | cu_attn_opt    | 8     | 48      | 110     | 0.81
qwen7 native          | flash_attn_v2  | 8     | 55      | 130     | 0.78
mixtral8 native       | flash_attn_v2  | 4     | 60      | 135     | 0.74
```
Morgan: notes: the llama3b->mixtral8 pairing shows a huge p99 tail and accept_rate collapsed to ~22%. enabling speculative decoding increased p95 by ~8-12ms on paired runs vs native.
Jin: interesting — acceptance drop smells like tokenizer mismatch with draft outputs being tokenized differently by the serving decoder. saw something similar with rope_scale changes before. any token align diffs?
Morgan: yes — diffs in byte offsets for some unicode sequences. small example: llama draft emits a combined token that mixtral tokenizer splits. acceptance heuristics (we require exact token-prefix match) fail.
Carlos: that explains the low accept_rate. two levers: (1) relax acceptance to fuzzy-match prefix (token overlap >= X) or (2) add a lightweight token remap table at pairing time. both have latency implications.
Priya: what's the latency cost for fuzzy acceptance?
Morgan: tested a simple overlap check implemented in C: +1.5–3ms p95 on those paired requests at batch=4. but full remap step (re-tokenize draft output) adds ~7–12ms depending on sequence length.
Jin: also saw KV cache warmup contributing to p99. when pairing cross-family we can't reuse compiled KV layout, so first few tokens pay heavy kernel-selection + alloc cost. profiler snippet: 
```
[perf] stage: handshake -> kernel_select (18ms) -> kv_alloc (22ms) -> decode_loop
```
Morgan: exact — kv_alloc + kernel_select spikes on warm connections. after warmup things stabilize. in long-running traffic it's fine, but our canary traffic (short-lived requests with speculative drafts) amplifies the tail.
Carlos: batching heuristics also mis-fire: speculative decoding spawns an extra follow-up request per draft candidate which reduces effective batch density. observed average batch occupancy drop from 3.7->2.1 under speculative=true. that increases per-token overhead.
Priya: so actionables?
Morgan: proposed short list: 1) add a tokenizer compatibility check in draft-pairing validator (cheap token-prefix + unicode-normalize) 2) introduce a KV-layout cache key so paired runs can reuse compatible layouts when family-compatible 3) add a lightweight fuzzy-accept path with config flag (experiment at 0.6 threshold) 4) instrument batch-occupancy per-route when speculative=true for 72h and collect p95 deltas.
Jin: + add a unit for rope_scale mismatch: when rope_scale differs by >10% between draft and decoder, mark as potential reject — rope mis-scale can change positional tokens and head activations.
Carlos: also put a small scheduler change: prefer consolidating speculative candidates into same micro-batch window for 50ms to keep occupancy. tradeoff increases tail latency for earliest requests but lowers p95 overall.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline note: uploaded test image infra/smoke-pairing:sha-7a3b — running canary on eng-runtime/smoke-pairing for next 30m :information_source:
Priya: can you open an issue with the numbers and attach the profiler traces? I can run the fuzzy-accept experiment if we toggle via runtime flags.
Morgan: created issue #3789 in backlog and uploaded trace+profiler snippets. linking in thread.
Jin: temporary mitigation: lower accept_threshold to 0.5 for mixed-family routes and enable tokenizer-normalize on input. will push a short-lived feature flag. monitor for hallucination/regressions.
Carlos: sounds good. I'll prototype the KV-layout-cache key in the runtime — key will include family fingerprint + head_dim + kv_dim + rope_scale. if mismatch, fallback.
Morgan: thanks all — summary: root cause = tokenizer alignment + KV/layout mismatch + batching density loss from speculative candidates. plan = small acceptance relax + tokenizer normalization + KV-layout reuse key + scheduler window. tagging @pri for the experiment. :thumbsup:
